newsitem.title: INDIA: Communist minister boosts PM before key India vote.
newsitem.headline: Communist minister boosts PM before key India vote.

text.p: A major crisis in Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet eased on Monday when a senior communist minister turned away from an opposition-led campaign to sack a state governor.

Home (Interior) Minister Indrajit Gupta, who had earlier joined the opposition in criticising Romesh Bhandari, governor of India's most populous Uttar Pradesh state, told the upper house of parliament he had no plans to sack the official.
The Lok Sabha, the lower house of parliament, was due to debate the issue later this week.

Gupta had joined hands with the rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) earlier this month when he told the Lok Sabha that Uttar Pradesh, directly ruled by Delhi for more than a year, was heading for "anarchy, chaos and destruction".
The BJP has been campaigning for Bhandari's dismissal, holding him responsible for a recent spurt in crime in Uttar Pradesh.
But on Monday, India's first communist minister in the federal cabinet backed down from his position in a sign of rapprochement with Deve Gowda, regarded as sympathetic to Bhandari.

"I don't want this subject of law and order to be taken so lightly and make it appear as a fight between two individuals," he said. "I don't want to descend to that level. It is only diverting the subject from the seriousness it deserves."

Gupta's remarks appeared to have thwarted the BJP's campaign to drive a wedge into the 15-party United Front coalition over the Bhandari issue, which had threatened to overshadow debate later this month on the government's annual budget.
The Lok Sabha was expected to vote on the budget for the 1997/98 financial year starting on April 1 after discussing and voting on Bhandari's future this week.

The Gupta-Bhandari standoff and the political uncertainty it provoked triggered heavy selling on the Delhi Stock Exchange on Monday. The bourse's benchmark index closed 34.17 points, or 4.13 percent, lower at 794.16 points.
Analysts said Gupta's remarks on Monday would help Deve Gowda take on the BJP in the budget vote later this month.

The BJP succeeded, however, in putting the issue of Uttar Pradesh on the federal parliament's agenda after lower house Speaker Purno Sangma ruled on Thursday that lawmakers would be told to vote on Bhandari's future.
